name: Pineyard.ai
summary: AI voice agents for the conversations businesses cannot afford to miss.
problem: A missed call can mean a missed opportunity. Pineyard helps businesses follow up with leads, recover lost revenue, and keep high-intent conversations moving.
approach: My work at Pineyard sits at the intersection of technical leadership and product presentation. I designed and built the website, translating a voice AI platform into a clear, approachable product experience.
decision: The website focuses on the business workflow: a lead arrives, an agent has a conversation, and the next step becomes clear. The visual language makes an invisible voice product understandable.
note: Pineyard is a team product. My role is Tech Lead; the company owns the platform code.

name: Credent
summary: A revenue-based credit marketplace with private financials and a public lending ledger.
problem: Lenders need evidence of a business’s ability to repay. Sharing the whole set of books reveals much more than that decision requires.
approach: Credent separates private revenue from public proof. A Noir circuit proves that a revenue threshold is met, while a hash-chained ledger records loans, settlements, and losses. A lockbox routes incoming payments to installments before releasing the operating balance.
decision: Privacy is an architectural boundary. Raw revenue stays in private tables, public endpoints are allow-listed, and on-chain inflows are aggregated across borrowers. Senior and junior tranches define how yield and losses flow through a pool.
note: A prototype on local chains and Solana devnet, with test-mode Stripe. It has not been audited and is not intended for real funds.

name: SafeHER
summary: Time-aware route planning that considers when you reach each street.
problem: The shortest route is not always the most practical one after dark. Lighting, open businesses, and street activity change over the course of a journey.
approach: SafeHER uses time-dependent A*: every edge is evaluated at its estimated arrival time. It brings together road geometry, lighting estimates, activity signals, nearby safe havens, and community reports.
decision: The system avoids publishing a danger map. It presents route-level guidance and tracks the source of estimates, allowing the experience to acknowledge incomplete data instead of assigning a permanent label to a neighbourhood.
note: A routing research prototype. Estimates are contextual signals, not a guarantee of personal safety.

name: StarForge
summary: Real celestial mechanics, rendered as publication-ready vector star charts.
problem: A star chart should be scientifically grounded and visually considered. Scientific plotting tools often leave the design work to the person using them.
approach: StarForge combines real ephemerides and the Hipparcos catalog with a composable Python API and an SVG rendering pipeline. Location, time, field of view, and styling all feed a reproducible output.
decision: Vector output keeps the result useful beyond a browser. Charts stay crisp in print, and the same engine can be used from a short Python script or the command line.
note: An open-source Python package for reproducible astronomical charts. The banner and example chart are from the project.

name: Avsarathi.ai
summary: A scheme-matching assistant that pairs conversational input with deterministic eligibility.
problem: Government support is only useful when the people it is intended for can find it, understand the conditions, and identify a channel partner.
approach: The documented pipeline separates three tasks: eligibility rules, semantic extraction from conversational input, and partner routing. The web portal explains why a person qualifies, estimates loan costs, and identifies eligible partners.
decision: The eligibility decision is deterministic. Language-model extraction helps structure free text; it does not replace the rules that determine qualification.
note: A hackathon project. The documented implementation focuses on NSFDC eligibility and partner routing.

name: Caret AI
summary: Quick AI access at the cursor, without leaving the task at hand.
problem: A small writing or editing task can become a context switch: copy text, open an AI app, enter a prompt, and bring the result back.
approach: Caret AI brings the interaction beside the cursor. Select text, press Shift twice, enter a prompt, and receive the result on the clipboard. The project also explores desktop appearance through a custom PySide6 theming library.
decision: The interaction starts from the application already in use. Keyboard access and clipboard output keep the utility lightweight and close to a real everyday workflow.
note: An early release. The linked repositories contain the app and its evolving website/release materials.

name: ConfigX
summary: A hierarchical data engine built around readable keypath queries.
problem: Configuration, application state, and structured metadata often end up behind different interfaces, even when the underlying task is navigating a hierarchy.
approach: ConfigX explores a shared interface through dot-separated keypaths and ConfigXQL. The alpha focuses on basic operations over branches and values, with persistence described through snapshots and a write-ahead log.
decision: The query surface makes hierarchy explicit. More ambitious features—AI-assisted queries, schema enforcement, and batch transactions—are described as future scope rather than capabilities of the current alpha.
note: Alpha software. AI reasoning, advanced wildcard queries, and other roadmap features are not presented as shipped.

name: Fusion
summary: An experimental programming language, from tokens to a working interpreter.
problem: Building a language is a way to understand the machinery behind every program: how source becomes structure, how expressions evaluate, and how errors reach the developer.
approach: Fusion implements a lexer, parser, and interpreter with variables, control flow, functions, lists, and tracebacks. It includes an interactive shell and supports running source files.
decision: The current release is an interpreter. LLVM compilation, concurrency, and higher-performance execution remain longer-term goals.
note: Experimental alpha. Performance, concurrency, and memory-safety aspirations are not benchmarked claims.

name: Snippify
summary: A Python library for saving, finding, and reusing code snippets.
problem: Useful snippets tend to disappear into old projects, scattered notes, and half-remembered files.
approach: Snippify captures Python objects or selected line ranges with metadata, lists saved snippets in formatted tables, and retrieves them by title or identifier.
decision: Capturing a snippet from an object or line range keeps the library close to the way developers already work. Search and retrieval are part of the same workflow.
note: A focused developer utility available as a Python package.
